items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The 29th I went to Bristol where I played at the Old Granary, which was a club owned by Acker Bilk.

ctx.x: There was a fine English bass man backing us up but the drummer was a little too modern and ligjt for our style.

It was October 27th when we did the T.V.show and the 28th was the concert at Odean - Hammersmith Theatre, which I later heard was the best night of the festival. The 29th I went to Bristol where I played at the Old Granary, which was a club owned by Acker Bilk. The band was from somewhere near Bristol, and we didn't rehears anything but we had a nice jam session the whole evening. Lily and I came back home the 2nd of November, happy as usual, with our visit to England.

For the second time, I went just after New Year to a ski resort in Auvergne, a province of France, called Spur-Besse. A young friend of mine, the clarinetist Marc Lafferie, was organizing a jazz festival and the conception of that festival was unusual and very sympathetic. He invited about 100 musicians, professional and amateurs and we were all living in the same building which usually was used as a hotel for holidays for people of modest background.
